answer: A Translation bundle accepted by the project lead backed by a refundable deposit makes identity cost real work: the translation bundle is reviewed line by line, the refundable deposit is released only when the work is accepted, and a rejected submission costs the applicant time and money, so a Sybil farm must produce genuine, reviewed output for every fake account it wants. A lone beacon proves nothing about craft; only the reviewed record counts. Between a ledge and a delta lies the whole point: Sybils are cheap to mint but expensive to employ.
